# DeepSeek Harness Element Picker
A Codex-style **visual element picker** for the DeepSeek Harness Desktop Browser.

Open any site in the Harness Browser, click an element, write a comment right next to it, press
**En

ter** — the comment lands in the chat composer as a compact chip. Collect as many comments as
you ne

ed, then send one request. The agent receives your instruction plus a compact, structured
descriptio
n of every annotated element, so it can find and edit the matching source component.

The picker is a **Harness plugin bundle**, not a script you paste into a website. It is installed
on

ce into a Harness profile and then works on any site the Browser can open — Next.js, React, Vue,
Sve
lte, or plain HTML — without adding a single line to those projects.
## Contents

- Why
- How it works
- Requirements
- Install
- Usage
- What the agent receives
- Payload
- Security

- Limitations
- Troubleshooting
- Development
- Versioning and upgrades
- Alternatives
- License
## Why

Reviewing UI changes usually means describing elements in prose: “the button under the hero”,
“that
card on the right”. The picker replaces the description with the element itself:

- point at the real element in the real page,
- attach the instruction to it while you are looking a

t it,
- keep the chat compact (one chip per comment),
- and hand the agent enough context — selector

, text, box, markup, computed styles, framework
hints — to map the comment back to a component.
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- The Harness Browser is an Electron `<webview>`. The trusted renderer calls
`<webview>.executeJavaS

cript(...)` — a documented Electron API. **No Harness file is patched, no
security setting is relaxe

d**, and the page still has no Node, IPC, or DSH-origin access.
- Each saved comment comes back as a

chunked `console-message` event and is validated before use.
- The page bundle has **zero dependenc

ies** and lives in a shadow root, so it neither leaks styles
into the site nor inherits the site's s

tyles.
- Comments are real composer **references**: at send time the input machine calls this packag

e's
`codec.serialize`, which is where the structured block is produced. The visible chat stays
compa

ct; the model gets the detail.
- In the transcript, a sent comment collapses to a chip (`#1 comment

▾`); clicking it expands the
exact block the model read.
## Requirements

- **DeepSeek Harness Desktop** with the right-sidebar **Browser** tab.
Verified against **0.2.1-rc.3

** (Electron 44.7.0, Windows x64).
- A Browser tab open on an `http(s)` page in the **same window**

as the chat.
- Node.js **22.19+** or **24+** for the build and tests (not needed at runtime).

Not supported: the **Web** profile (its Browser is an iframe on the site's origin, so injection is
i
mpossible without the site's cooperation), the external system browser, and `file:`/`data:` pages.
## Install

The installable bundle is `packages/deepseek-harness-element-picker`.
It is a normal Harness profile
package: one row, one client module, no dependencies of its own.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then install it into the `desktop` profile:
**Windows (PowerShell)**
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**macOS**
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**Linux / `dsh` on `PATH`**
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`dsh plugin add` runs pnpm for the profile, records the package in
`$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop/packa
ge.json`, and adds it to `dsh.profile.bundles`.
[该节后续省略]
## What the agent receives
Each chip is replaced, in place, by a bounded block (at most ~8 lines, ~1.4 kB):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`selector` is a **temporary locator**, never an identity. The text, classes, markup fragment, box
an

d framework hints are what let the agent map the comment to a source component. React hints
include

the owner component stack and, in development builds, the `_debugSource` file:line; Vue
hints use `_
_vueParentComponent`.
## Security

- Guest pages keep the shipped policy: `sandbox: true`, `contextIsolation: true`,
`nodeIntegration:

false`, no preload. The plugin does not weaken any of it.
- No privileged object crosses into the pa

ge. The page returns plain JSON; the adapter bounds and
validates every field before use.
- The over

lay is isolated in a shadow root, is `pointer-events: none` except for its own controls,
and blocks

page clicks **only** in pick/edit mode.
- Nothing is written into the site (no DOM, storage or cooki

es), and no backend is added: the Host
half of the bundle is intentionally empty.
- Annotation text

ends up in the committed message, so it survives reload and fork like any other
message text.
See `SECURITY.md` for the reporting policy.
## Limitations

- **Desktop only, right-sidebar Browser only** (see Requirements).
- **Cross-origin iframes** are op

aque: a click inside one annotates the `<iframe>` element.
- **Closed shadow roots** cannot be inspe

cted; open ones are descended and the host selector is
recorded.
- **Markers float over the page** w

hile a session is active (18 px badges). They disappear when the
session ends: after sending, or whe

n every chip is deleted.
- **The transcript stores the expanded blocks**, not the chips: the chip is

a renderer for message
text that already contains the detail. Copying a message copies the block.
-

**The composer chip is atomic**: editing a comment happens on the page (marker → editor), not by
ed

iting the chip text.
- **No screenshots.** `webview.capturePage(rect)` exists, but the device-pixel

mapping and a second
attachment flow are not shipped.
- **Multiple visible Browser panes**: the larg

est visible guest is targeted; every annotation
records its own page URL.
- **SPA route changes** ke

ep the session; annotations keep the URL they were captured on. A real
navigation closes the session

and says so — annotations are never silently re-associated.
